text:
maria: Hey team, Mistral (dedicated capacity) just opened a ticket — they're seeing sustained token-per-second SLO violations during bursts. They say burst credits exist but admission keeps rejecting requests. Repro as soon as they hit ~320 TPS.
jamal: Can you paste the admission controller logs and the client error payload?
mar ia: oops typo — sending logs now.
maria: Logs: ```
[2026-02-22T18:12:10Z] admission: admit_check: client=mistral-app-01, req_id=abc123, tps=328, burst_credits=1200, headroom=0.15
[2026-02-22T18:12:10Z] admission: decision=deny, reason=insufficient_headroom, available_tokens=0
[2026-02-22T18:12:11Z] quota: deduct_failed: race_detected
```
alex: interesting — `burst_credits=1200` but `available_tokens=0` suggests the headroom or admission accounting might have a race with the autoscaler. What is their headroom config?
maria: their dedicated config in console (redacted): ```yaml
capacity_plan: dedicated-gpu-4
burst: { credits: 1200, window_s: 60 }
admission: { headroom_pct: 15, min_capacity: 1 }
autoscale: { target_util: 0.75, cooldown_s: 90 }
```
paige: Do we have traces or a span id for the deny? also did autoscaler kick during the burst?
maria: span id: span-0x9b7f. Autoscaler logs: ```
[2026-02-22T18:12:05Z] autoscale: scale_up_triggered -> new_pods=2 (from 1)
[2026-02-22T18:12:35Z] autoscale: scale_stabilized at 3 pods
[2026-02-22T18:12:40Z] pod-2: ready; init_kv_cache_miss=high
```
jamal: The timeline shows admission denials before pods are ready, so admission logic isn't accounting for transient warmup. If KV cache warmup takes time, available_tokens can be 0 until pod is warmed. Could be noisy neighbor or slow cache preload.
paige: Agreed. Another angle: check token accounting ledger — `quota: deduct_failed: race_detected` is suspicious. Maybe concurrent deducts from multiple in-flight admission checks.
alex: Can you run a reproducer? curl with token header at 350 TPS for 30s and capture 429s. Use this snippet: ```bash
for i in {1..350}; do curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' & done; wait
```
maria: ran it — payload shows 429s with body: `{ "error": "admission_denied", "reason": "insufficient_headroom" }` consistently until ~18:12:40 when some succeed.
support-bot: Ticket #INC-3342 created for Mistral (added to support queue).
sre-bot: Alert fired: `dedicated.admission.slo_violation` (threshold 300 TPS sustained over 60s).
jamal: Quick checklist: 1) verify ledger consistency (single-writer or CAS), 2) add temp warmup headroom (e.g., +20%) while autoscaler transitions, 3) consider KV cache prefetch strategy, 4) run per-pod token buckets to avoid global race.
alex: For immediate customer relief propose: - increase admission.headroom_pct from 15 -> 30 (temporary) - enable short-term burst top-up: +600 credits - add a canary rollout so they can test without full traffic shift
paige: Long-term: implement admission backpressure that accounts for pods in Pending/Initializing; treat them as unavailable until warm. Also add a per-request trace tag to track which pod honored the token.
maria: I'll schedule the headroom bump and top-up now and follow up with the customer. Thanks. :thumbsup:
alex: Also capture kernel/GPU utilization during the bursts — autoscaler shouldn't spin up if utilization is low (noisy neighbor maybe hogging memory/cache).
jamal: I'll open a follow-up infra ticket to add a short-lived metric for `kv_cache_fill_ratio` and `token_ledger_ops_per_s` to help diagnose this in future.
paige: sounds good. keep me posted, I'll prepare a postmortem template if this recurs.
maria: will do. pinging customer with repro steps and temporary top-up.
